---
title: "Combinatorial Optimization and Constraint Programming"
subtitle: "Modelling and solving CSP and COP in MiniZinc"
---

A collection of mathematical models solving Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSP) and Constrained Optimization Problems (COP) with MiniZinc, focused on search space reduction, symmetry breaking and performance benchmarking. Built for the Intelligent Systems Techniques course (Técnicas de los Sistemas Inteligentes, 2025-26) of the Computer Science and Mathematics double degree at the University of Granada.

[View source on GitHub](https://github.com/laurasalop03/combinatorial-optimization-csp){.btn .btn-outline-secondary}

## Algorithmic highlights

- **Symmetry breaking and pruning**: enforced strict lexicographical ordering on matrix based search spaces, collapsing 8 symmetric variants (reflections and rotations) into a single representative to speed up solver convergence.
- **Multi-objective optimization**: transformed multi-objective knapsack problems into single-function COPs using a weighted sum with order-of-magnitude scaling, to enforce a strict lexicographic priority between objectives.
- **Data structure optimization**: re-architected time based scheduling models (for example NBA back-to-back constraints, sequential assembly) to use 1D parallel arrays indexed by time instead of sparse 2D matrices, sharply reducing the search space and memory footprint.
- **Scalability benchmarking**: profiled search heuristics (`first_fail`, `indomain_min`) and documented the exponential time blow-up for state spaces where $N \ge 5$.

## Why it is relevant to quant work

Portfolio construction and allocation are constrained optimization problems, often multi-objective (return versus risk versus cost). This project shows exactly that skill set: formulating objectives and constraints, encoding priorities with weighted sums, and reasoning quantitatively about solver performance and scalability.

## Tech

MiniZinc, Constraint Logic Programming.
